items.title: 52222_Marshall Royal oral history interview
items.q: William Randolph Hearst never came on the Avenue in his life

ctx.x: William Randolph Hearst -- it wasn't William Randolph Hearst at all. Now, you can get it straight from the horse's mouth now. George Hearst was a friend of mine and he used to come out to Sebastian's Cotton Club and ask me to take him down on Central Avenue to enjoy himself down there

at the after-hours places. So I knew George Hearst very well. William Randolph Hearst never came on the Avenue in his life because he was from some sort of affliction -- he was sort of semi-invalid. He didn't get around. He had elephantitis or something, some kind of way. He was really not a healthy man. The only thing he was really healthy in was money. But George used to come down and he was considered as being the black sheep of the family.
